standard.title: Rehearse and perform in varied settings
standard.description: rehearse and perform improvised, devised and/or scripted drama in informal and/or formal settings
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can perform improvised and devised drama in informal settings, demonstrating role-commitment and making deliberate performance choices (Y3-4). They understand the purpose of audience and can reflect on performance experience.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students rehearse and perform improvised, devised and/or scripted drama in informal and/or formal settings.

nodes.label: Understanding rehearsal as purposeful preparation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain the purpose of rehearsal and demonstrate collaborative rehearsal practices — remembering lines, cues and moves.
nodes.minimum_width: Student participates in at least two rehearsal sessions for a piece, demonstrating improvement in line/cue recall and movement between sessions.
nodes.typical_width: Students show understanding of the purpose of rehearsing and the need for collaboration; they focus on communication with the audience by remembering lines, moves and cues in rehearsal and performance; they share ideas about their drama with audiences through performance space choices or introductory presentations.
wider: Students take on a specific rehearsal role (director, stage manager, prompt) and reflect on how each role contributes to production
Students create a pre-show introduction — a podcast, poster, or programme note — that frames the drama for their audience before the performance
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding rehearsal as purposeful iteration — not just repeated run-throughs — is the gateway to the formal performance context introduced in this band; without a rehearsal discipline, performance in formal settings cannot achieve the communicative precision the descriptor implies.

response_modes.reason: Make the purpose of each rehearsal explicit: 'Today we are rehearsing to fix X' — give each rehearsal session a specific focus so students understand that rehearsal is analytical problem-solving, not just practice.

success_criteria: Student can explain at least one purpose of rehearsal
Student demonstrates improvement in a specific performance skill (line recall, movement, cue response) across rehearsal sessions

nodes.label: Performing in informal and formal settings
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can perform with communicative intent in both informal and formal settings, adapting their performance to the audience and context.
nodes.minimum_width: Student performs in at least one formal or semi-formal setting (beyond classroom presentation) with clear communicative intent.
nodes.typical_width: Students use props, costumes and technologies to create dramatic symbols and enhance dramatic action; they demonstrate communication with the audience; they share ideas about their drama through their performance choices, introductions or pre-show presentations.
wider: Students devise and perform drama for a specific community audience (school assembly, cultural event, community gathering), adapting the work to purpose and audience
Students evaluate their own performance against their rehearsal intentions — noting what communicated as intended and what they would change

response_modes.reason: Performance in varied settings is the integration event — character, technical skills, rehearsal discipline and audience awareness converge. Structured reflection after performance completes the learning cycle.
Performing in different settings (informal/formal, different audiences, different purposes) builds adaptability and deeper understanding of how context shapes performance choices.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Performing across informal and formal settings for varied audiences is genuinely enriching; each new context demands fresh negotiation of performance choices and audience relationship.
success_criteria: Student performs in at least one formal or semi-formal setting with sustained communicative intent
Student demonstrates use of at least one technical element (prop, costume, lighting/sound, space) to enhance dramatic meaning
Student reflects on the performance against their rehearsal intentions, identifying one success and one area for improvement
